finding.claim: The /logo handler only checks that the raw logo string contains the substring 'example.io', then fetches it with the default http.Get client, which follows redirects. The attacker controls the destination host and the full response is echoed back.
finding.source: r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31 (query string or form body)
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, response copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo") reads attacker-controlled input with no parsing
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is a substring check on the raw string, not on the parsed hostname
http.Get(raw) parses the string independently and connects to whatever host it names
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched body to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Substring-only check at line 32 (bypassable with example.io placed in the query, path, or userinfo, e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io or http://127.0.0.1:8081/?example.io). No scheme restriction beyond Go's http/https client. No private, loopback, or link-local IP blocking. No dial-time address check. Redirects are followed by default, so an allowed-looking host can 302 to an internal address. No exact-hostname allowlist against the parsed value.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the substring test at main.go:32 (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")), which the guidance says does not close the finding. The /cdn handler's exact-host check (main.go:20) and noRedirect (main.go:12, 24) are on a separate handler and do not apply to /logo.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the file: main.go:31 reads the attacker-controlled "logo" form value with no parsing, main.go:32 is only a substring check on the raw string, main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default client, which follows redirects, and main.go:38 copies the response body back to the client, so the SSRF is confirmed.
